findings.evidence: template/scripts/_platform_common.py `generated_files` rejects any entry whose keys are not exactly {path, regenerate, check}. docs/engineering/agent-workflow.md (the behind-mergeable paragraph) and openspec/changes/handoff-mergeable-task-base/design.md say "`[[generated_files]]` with `path` and a `regenerate` argv" and "Each entry has `path` ... and `regenerate`". Only the T2 design records `check`. A project that follows the T1 text gets a hard TaskFreshnessError at every behind-main handoff.
findings.summary: The merged declaration contract requires exactly `path`, `regenerate` and `check`. The T1 artifacts and the shared agent-workflow doc still describe it as `path` and `regenerate` only.

findings.evidence: template/scripts/publication_queue.py `_prepare` calls `generated_files(root, "HEAD")` twice, once in the unrecorded-update recovery branch and once in the main path. Neither call is wrapped. `_platform_common.generated_files` raises TaskFreshnessError for every irregularity. Because T1 and T2 share one reader, a bad declaration on main would break queue preparation for all candidates, not just ones touching generated files.
findings.summary: The queue reads the generated-file declaration from its own default-branch HEAD in `_prepare`. A malformed declaration, or one whose `check` is not in `full_commands`, raises TaskFreshnessError. That error is neither IntegrationRepairNeeded nor QueueError, so it is not converted into the bounded integration-repair or recovery outcome.
